speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That abdominal tenderness and distension are serious findings. Has the baby passed any stool or gas recently, and does the vomiting persist or seem to stop completely?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the absence of fever, vomiting, and diarrhea helps rule out infection. Given the feeding difficulties, distension, and severe pain on palpation, has the baby passed any stool, and if so, was it green or contained white, seed-like material?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia (likely jejunal or ileal).

The absence of stool despite significant abdominal distension and pain suggests a complete obstruction proximal to the colon. I will request a lower limb X-ray to confirm the absence of gas in the rectum and look for specific signs like the "double bubble" sign.
